description: We are a team interested in space exploration and solving real-world problems. We are looking for members with skills in coding, software development, data analysis, and design. We welcome team members who enjoy learning, sharing ideas, and working together.
summary: Lunar Horizons is an interactive geospatial characterization tool that cross-references NASA lunar and Martian orbital datasets with Earth observation data to identify under-studied terrestrial analog sites for future permanent bases and landing missions. While existing analog sites like the Atacama Desert and Haughton Crater are widely used, they do not cover all extreme thermal, geological, and subsurface conditions required for sustained human exploration. By analyzing topography, mineral spectra, surface temperature, and subsurface structures, Lunar Horizons scores and maps four high-potential Earth analogs—including Antarctica’s Sør Rondane Mountains, Australia’s Undara Lava Tubes, Botswana’s Makgadikgadi Pans, and the Tibetan Plateau—helping mission teams test rovers, habitats, and resource-extraction hardware before launch.
details:
What It Does & How It Works Lunar Horizons is a geospatial characterization and comparison platform designed to identify under-studied terrestrial analog sites for future permanent Moon bases and Mars landing missions. Rather than relying solely on heavily studied sites like the Atacama Desert or Haughton Crater, our system cross-references lunar and Martian orbital telemetry—including elevation, slope, surface temperature extremes, mineral composition, and subsurface radar/gravity anomalies—against global Earth observation datasets to score and map high-fidelity terrestrial matches.

Key Terrestrial Analogs Identified

1. Lunar South Pole (Shackleton Crater Rim)

Sør Rondane Mountains, Antarctica: Shares extreme cryogenic temperatures, katabatic winds, high-illumination ridges adjacent to permanently shadowed terrain, and dry regolith conditions ideal for testing thermal-control systems and solar power arrays.

2. Lunar Lava Tubes (Marius Hills)

Undara Lava Tubes, Australia & Jeju Island, South Korea: Replicates basaltic shield volcanism and intact subsurface cavern networks critical for testing radiation shielding, autonomous cave-mapping rovers, and subsurface habitat deployment.

3. Mars Ancient Lakebeds (Jezero Crater)

Makgadikgadi Pans, Botswana: Matches hyper-arid evaporite salt flats, sulfate/clay mineralogy, and wind-sculpted yardangs for testing sample-caching drills and biosignature sensors.

4. Mars Mid-Latitude Subsurface Ice → Aksai Chin / Tibetan Plateau Permafrost: Simulates high UV flux, thin/cold arid conditions, and buried water-ice tables beneath dry regolith for In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) water-extraction trials.

Tools, Data & Development

We synthesized open orbital datasets from NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO), GRAIL, and NASA Earthdata (Landsat 9, SRTM, ASTER GDEM) using geospatial GIS mapping and multi-criteria scoring matrices to normalize environmental parameters across planetary bodies.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Selecting safe landing sites and sustainable base locations is one of the highest-risk phases of planetary exploration. Lunar Horizons gives mission architects, rover engineers, and analog researchers an accessible, data-backed catalog to test hardware, mobility systems, and life-support protocols in realistic Earth environments before launch.
